description:
Commerce Wars
v0.3.1 - late-game market and military pressure - for Starsector 0.98a

Download

CommerceWars-0.3.1.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save. LunaLib optional (full in-game config menu).

Pogo's explanation

This one you may want to configure yourself, but I'm pretty happy with the current default values. Thresholds for a Trade Grievance:

Both you and they have a minimum 10% share of a market (e.g. fuel production)
You must have at least equal to their share or more

For a military grievance you must have at least 80% of their strength for them to get worried. They will only issue ultimatums and raid you if they have the military strength to do so. if they dont they will try to form a coalition with another faction who is their ally and also has a grievance. If even combined they are not strong enough they will stay silent. The end result of this is eventually everyone will form a coalition with Heg in an attempt to bring you down, leading to potentially 5 simultaneous strikes spread across you colonies simultaneously. Note similar to colony crises none of these events effect your actual faction relations, unless of course you tac bomb them back.

If the strikes fail they escalate. If they succeed they chill out as usually this means your market share will be disrupted and they are no longer concerned with your existence. Escalation can lead to events like them stealing nanoforges and other colony items. But at lower levels will just be a tac bombing and/or industry raid.

There is an additional feature of the mod which if you sat bomb a faction essentially gives them permission to sat bomb you back. So all subsequent raids will be sat bombs.

Claude's explanation

Factions push back when you dominate their export markets or the sector military balance. Any faction whose export business you muscle in on develops a grievance.
Market shares are recomputed weekly from the same export numbers on the commodity info screens; a faction gets a grievance when it is a significant producer and your share rivals theirs.
Each aggrieved faction gets a colony-crisis-style intel screen with a 0-600 resentment bar: diplomatic warning at 200, formal ultimatum at 400, enforcement fleets at 600.
Compliance is automatic - reduce your contested share any way you like (downgrade, demolish, lose it to a rival, or bomb the customer) and the dispute cools on its own.
Ultimatum options: Comply (lose the share), Settle (pay down resentment), Commission (fly their flag), or Defy.
Enforcement fleets are sized to overmatch your actual defenses, your own fleet included, bounded only by the faction's real military-industrial capacity. Disrupting their war industry shrinks what they can send.
Adaptive strikes: fleets shell open strong defenses, then disrupt the grievance industries one landing at a time, falling back to bombardment or stockpile raids. Every raid posts a fleet-by-fleet operations report.
Coalitions: factions too weak to press demands alone pool behind a leader and strike multiple fronts with synchronized arrivals.
Sabotage window: knock out a strike's staging military base or high command during its planning phase to abort the contingent.
Item heists: at high escalation a contingent storms the vault for an installed nanoforge or synchrotron; stolen items install on their markets and can be raided back.
Ground truth: raiders take or disrupt only what they can actually reach, using the same raid-strength math the player faces (planetary shield and garrison marines included).
Strength gate: only a faction that can crack the target colony presses demands; outgrow every plausible coalition and the demands stop.
Counterplay ladder: defeat the strike fleets, abort at the source, tac-bomb their production or war industry, settle/comply/commission, or sat-bomb the competitor (which creates a permanent no-quarter vendetta).
Total War option (off by default): strips story-critical protection so any world can be destroyed and factions eliminated.
For Starsector 0.98a. LunaLib optional. Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save; removing mid-save is not supported. Defers to vanilla colony crises.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
Useful Planetary Shield — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

Disclaimer: This post and these mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.

aiDescription: Factions develop grievances when you rival their market shares or outmatch their military strength. They escalate from diplomatic warnings to ultimatums and finally to enforcement fleets, coalitions, and raids that target your colonies and industries. You can comply, settle, commission, defy, or counterattack, with options to sabotage staging bases or steal back raided items.
